title: Marketing Creative Agency Rates: Budgeting Contract Upkeep for Your Agency Office
seoTitle: Marketing Creative Agency Rates: Office Cleaning Cost & Budget
metaDescription: Marketing creative agency rates for cleaning run $0.09–$0.20 per sq ft per visit. See monthly budgets for 1,800–8,000 sq ft agencies and price yours now.
excerpt: Creative agencies pay national per-visit cleaning rates of roughly $0.09 to $0.20 per sq ft, but kitchens, photo studios, and client-facing lounges change the math. Here is how restroom density, event traffic, and frequency shape a realistic monthly and annual budget.
quickAnswer: Marketing and creative agencies typically pay $0.12–$0.20 per sq ft per visit under 2,500 sq ft and $0.09–$0.15 per sq ft between 2,500 and 9,999 sq ft, plus $15–$30 per restroom and $12–$25 for kitchen sanitation per visit. A 3,500 sq ft agency on hardwood cleaned three times weekly budgets about $4,750–$8,100 per month, while an 8,000 sq ft agency with daily service runs $16,300–$27,800. Agencies with frequent client events or an in-house content studio should plan for daily weekday service.

blocks.text: What Makes Agency Offices Cost More (or Less) to Clean

Marketing and creative agencies run some of the most variable office floors in commercial real estate. One agency is a quiet 1,800 sq ft suite of strategists; another is an 8,000 sq ft loft with a bar-style kitchen, a podcast booth, a product-photography cyc wall, and a Thursday client happy hour. Square footage alone does not predict cleaning cost; usage does.

Three features drive agency budgets above a standard office. Kitchens and coffee bars that function like small cafés, with espresso grounds, oat-milk spills, and a full dishwasher, add sanitation time every visit. Hard floors chosen for aesthetics, especially engineered hardwood and polished concrete, need specific products. And event traffic, from pitches to launch parties, creates periodic spikes that a standard schedule cannot absorb.

The scenarios below follow the calculator's national model: square footage times the bracket rate, times the flooring and frequency multipliers, plus restrooms and add-ons per visit, multiplied by visits per month based on 4.33 weeks per month.

blocks.text: On a monthly per-sq-ft basis, the boutique agency lands near $0.60–$1.01, the 3,500 sq ft agency near $1.36–$2.32, and the 8,000 sq ft agency near $2.04–$3.47. Weekly service looks inexpensive, but it rarely holds up in an agency with a working kitchen; most firms that start weekly add a second visit within a quarter.

blocks.title: Benchmark: Restroom Density and Kitchen Load
blocks.text: Agencies typically have one restroom per 2,000 to 3,000 sq ft and often a single-occupant all-gender restroom near the lounge. Expect $15–$30 per restroom per visit. Kitchens used by more than 20 people daily usually justify the full $25 breakroom add-on rather than the $12 low end.
Traffic Wear Patterns in Creative Offices

items: Lounge and collaboration zones: soft seating collects crumbs and coffee drips; weekly upholstery vacuuming prevents staining.
Kitchen island and coffee bar: the highest soil-load area in most agencies, needing degreasing and floor mopping every visit.
Photo and video studio: cyc walls and seamless paper areas need dust control without wet contact; crews vacuum only.
Entry and reception: client-facing; hardwood here benefits from daily dust mopping and weekly neutral-cleaner damp mopping.
Event aftermath: post-event cleans billed as extra visits, often at the specialty hourly band of $55–$95.

blocks.text: Hardwood carries a 1.08 multiplier because crews must use low-moisture methods and wood-safe cleaners; mixed floors add 1.05 for dual tooling. Budget a quarterly deep floor program at $0.03–$0.06 per sq ft per month amortized, about $105–$210 per month for 3,500 sq ft, to protect the finish in high-traffic lanes.

items.name: Fewer than 12 people, light kitchen use
items.text: Weekly service (4.33 visits per month) with staff handling dishes; add a mid-week restroom touch-up if feedback slips.

items.name: 12 to 35 people with an active kitchen
items.text: Three visits per week (13 per month) is the sweet spot; the 0.95 multiplier trims per-visit cost compared with twice weekly.

items.name: 35-plus people, client events, or a content studio
items.text: Daily weekday service (21.65 visits per month) at the 0.90 multiplier, plus pre-priced post-event visits.

items.name: Hybrid schedules
items.text: If the office is busy Tuesday through Thursday, schedule visits on Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday night to reset after peak days instead of cleaning an empty Monday office.

blocks.text: Equipment Choices That Affect Your Bid

Agencies with open lofts and daytime hours benefit from quiet cordless backpack vacuums so porters can work during the day. The Karcher BV 5/1 runs at about 62 dBA with a 1.3 gallon capacity and fleece plus HEPA filtration at 11.7 lb, quiet enough near meeting pods. The Makita XCV17Z is lighter at 9.9 lb with a 2.0 L HEPA-filtered body on the 36V LXT platform for spot passes between meetings, while the Milwaukee M18 FUEL 3-in-1 converts to handheld for vents and shelving with a 1 gal HEPA-filtered canister. Vendors equipped with quiet cordless gear can often offer daytime porter coverage that reduces night-crew hours.

blocks.title: Pre-Price Event Cleanups
blocks.text: Ask bidders for a fixed post-event price tied to headcount bands, for example under 50 guests and 50 to 120 guests. That avoids surprise invoices after launch parties and lets account teams build cleanup into client event budgets.

faqs.q: Why does my weekly agency quote not equal four visits per month?
faqs.a: Vendors bill on 52 weeks divided by 12, or about 4.333 weeks per month, so weekly service equals about 4.33 visits monthly. Over a year, that captures the extra visits in months with five cleaning days. Bids that multiply by four look cheaper but usually reconcile later through extra charges.

faqs.q: Should kitchen dishwashing be included in an agency cleaning contract?
faqs.a: Standard breakroom sanitation covers counters, sinks, appliance exteriors, and high-touch pulls. Loading and unloading dishwashers, cleaning espresso machines, and clearing refrigerators are usually excluded or priced separately. If your team expects those tasks, list them in the scope and expect the add-on to land at the high end of $12 to $25 per visit or more.

faqs.q: What insurance should an agency require from its cleaning vendor?
faqs.a: Request a certificate of insurance with $1 million per occurrence general liability, statutory workers compensation, and a fidelity bond covering employee theft. Agencies storing client products, camera gear, or prototypes should confirm care, custody, and control coverage and list the agency and landlord as additional insureds.

faqs.q: Are green cleaning products worth requiring in a creative agency?
faqs.a: For most agencies, yes. Green Seal or UL ECOLOGO certified products reduce odor and VOC complaints in open lofts with limited ventilation, and many agency clients ask about sustainability practices. Certified concentrates usually cost about the same per use as conventional cleaners.

faqs.q: What is usually excluded from a standard agency scope?
faqs.a: Common exclusions include moving or cleaning set props and camera equipment, washing dishes, exterior windows, carpet and upholstery extraction outside a scheduled program, post-event cleanup, and biohazard response under OSHA bloodborne pathogen rules. Each should be explicitly excluded or priced so invoices stay predictable.
